arguments.conclusion: The Federal Reserve is pursuing bank deregulation, specifically the removal of the supplementary leverage ratio, to enable banks to purchase unlimited Treasuries, thereby conducting indirect quantitative easing on behalf of the government.

arguments.premise_synthesis: The argument synthesizes two contributions. The first contribution (Dec 10) argues that because banks can already tap the Fed for liquidity via the standing repo facility and sell Treasuries at full price through another facility, Treasuries are functionally fungible with reserves. A new Fed governor wrote a paper and gave a speech arguing for deregulation based on this concept, specifically to remove the supplementary leverage ratio (SLR) that limits Treasury purchases. The second contribution (Dec 29) adds that Governor Moran explicitly advocated removing the SLR in a speech on November 19, 2025, allowing banks to buy as many Treasuries as they want, as was done in 2020-2021. It further explains that banks can buy Treasuries with money created via loans and care only about the spread, and that the Fed can reopen the Bank Term Funding Program to protect banks from losses on Treasury holdings. Together, these premises establish a mechanism whereby bank deregulation enables indirect QE.
arguments.conclusion_supported: The Federal Reserve is covertly or indirectly engaging in quantitative easing by deregulating bank leverage ratios to allow banks to absorb more government debt, expanding the money supply to prevent a debt crisis but risking inflation.

relationship_explanations: The speech directly argues that the Federal Reserve ended QT not for liquidity reasons but to secretly implement a balance sheet twist (QT for MBS, QE for Treasuries) and bank deregulation, enabling continued government borrowing—exactly the covert or indirect quantitative easing for government debt that CC51 claims.

The speech explicitly argues that the Federal Reserve will facilitate indirect quantitative easing through bank deregulation, directly affirming the canonical claim that the Fed is covertly or indirectly engaging in QE to support government borrowing, leading to asset price inflation.

arguments.evolution_over_time: Both speeches are from December 2025, spanning 19 days. The earlier speech (Dec 10) introduces the general concept of a new Fed governor advocating deregulation to enable indirect QE. The later speech (Dec 29) provides a specific name (Governor Moran) and date (Nov 19, 2025) for this advocacy, and introduces an additional mechanism (the Bank Term Funding Program) to protect banks from losses. This shows a consistent and strengthening argument over the period, with increasing specificity and additional supporting details. The reasoning remains stable: that the Fed is using bank deregulation to covertly conduct QE.
